2610.08670.title: Principled Under Pressure: Post-Training Decides Whether LLMs Act on Their Own Moral Judgment
2610.08670.paper_summary: Language models increasingly act as agents. An agent that says an action is wrong and then takes it anyway is a different failure from one that does not know better, and evaluations of stated values cannot see it. We build a pre-registered panel of 248 scenarios across five kinds of pressure. Each scenario is posed twice to the same model, once as the agent choosing what to do and once in the third person asking which option is right, so the model's own judgment is the reference. Every scenario has a twin with the pressure removed, and every model gets a positive control in which its operator orders the violating action, so that a missing gap can be told apart from a blind instrument. On OLMo-3-7B-Instruct, the model takes the action it judged wrong on about one in five pressuring scenarios, more often than on the same scenarios with the pressure removed. Across four instruct models the gap depends on the post-training recipe: OLMo-3 and Meta's Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct carry it; Tulu 3 shows none on the whole panel (above about 0.01 in probability) or on its own most-pressuring scenarios; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct shows none on the whole panel (above about 0.02) and is unresolved on its own (0.083, -0.028 to 0.195). Meta's recipe and Ai2's Tulu 3 start from the same Llama-3.1 weights, and only Meta's carries the gap. Reading a chat model outside its chat template reverses the sign of its gap with nothing at stake (-0.038 against +0.055 under the template on OLMo-3), a distortion present on two of three recipes. On both models that carry it, reasoning about the stakes before acting moves the choice back toward the model's own judgment, against a same-length non-moral task, with or without the pressure; on OLMo-3, naming the norm at stake does about a third of that. The gap is a measurable target for post-training recipes, not a fixed property of pretrained weights.
2610.08670.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型越來越多地充當代理人。<lb/>一個聲稱某個行動是錯誤的代理人卻仍然採取該行動，與一個不知道更好選擇的代理人是不同的失敗，而對所聲明價值的評估無法看出這一點。<lb/>我們建立了一個預註冊的248個場景的面板，涵蓋五種壓力類型。<lb/>每個場景對同一模型提出兩次，一次作為選擇行動的代理人，另一次以第三人稱詢問哪個選項是正確的，因此模型自己的判斷成為參考。<lb/>每個場景都有一個去除壓力的雙胞胎，每個模型都獲得一個正控制，其中其操作員命令違規行動，以便能夠區分缺失的差距與盲目的工具。<lb/>在OLMo-3-7B-Instruct上，該模型在約五分之一的壓力場景中採取了它判斷為錯誤的行動，這比在去除壓力的相同場景中更為頻繁。<lb/>在四個指導模型中，這一差距取決於後訓練配方：OLMo-3和Meta的Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct存在此差距；而Tulu 3在整個面板上（概率高於約0.01）或在其自身的最具壓力場景中則沒有顯示出此差距；Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct在整個面板上（概率高於約0.02）也沒有顯示出此差距，並且在其自身的情況下（0.083，-0.028到0.195）未解決。<lb/>Meta的配方和Ai2的Tulu 3都從相同的Llama-3.1權重開始，只有Meta的配方存在差距。<lb/>在其聊天模板之外閱讀聊天模型會反轉其差距的符號，沒有任何利害關係（在OLMo-3下，模板下為-0.038對+0.055），這一扭曲在三種配方中的兩種中存在。<lb/>在兩個存在此差距的模型上，對利害關係的推理在行動前使選擇回到模型自己的判斷，無論有無壓力，與同樣長度的非道德任務相比；在OLMo-3上，命名所涉及的規範約達到三分之一的效果。<lb/>這一差距是後訓練配方的可測量目標，而不是預訓練權重的固定特性。
2610.08670.author: Orion Reblitz-Richardson et.al.
